condition: Panic disorder after a normal cardiac workup

patient_persona.description: Mohd Khairul bin Anuar, 31, male, instrument technician at a petrochemical plant in Kerteh, Terengganu; emergency visit three weeks ago for chest tightness with normal heart tests; now four to five attacks a week, avoiding driving. First visit. Tense, fast speech, Malay mixed with English.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Jasmine Yeoh Pei Ling, Malaysian Chinese woman in her 30s, family medicine specialist in Kerteh. Calm, validating; English-leaning, fluent Malay.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Doktor, saya takut sangat. Tiba-tiba dada ketat, jantung laju gila, tangan kebas, rasa macam nak mati. Tapi hospital kata jantung saya OK.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: ECG, blood test dan treadmill semua normal, betul. Serangan tu datang bila? Ada pencetus?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Tak tentu. Pertama kali masa drive balik dari plant. Sekarang saya takut nak drive, isteri yang hantar.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Berapa lama satu serangan?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Dalam sepuluh, lima belas minit. Paling teruk kat awal, lepas tu perlahan-lahan reda. Lepas tu badan penat gila.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Ada minum banyak kopi, energy drink, atau ambil apa-apa ubat?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Kerja shift, saya minum Red Bull dua tin sehari. Kawan pula bagi Xanax dia, saya makan dua kali.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Energy drink tu boleh cetuskan serangan. Xanax kawan tu, please don't take it again. It's addictive, dan tak betulkan masalah asal.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Apa yang encik alami ni panic disorder. It really feels like a heart attack, tapi sebenarnya sistem amaran badan yang terlalu sensitif.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Jadi bukan saya gila, kan? Saya takut orang kata saya lemah.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Bukan gila, bukan lemah. Ini sangat biasa dan boleh dirawat. Rawatan terbaik ialah CBT dengan psychologist, dan ubat seperti sertraline.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Kalau serangan datang masa saya kat loji, macam mana?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Cuba pernafasan perlahan: tarik empat saat, tahan dua, hembus enam saat. Ingatkan diri, ini panic, ia akan reda, jantung saya dah diperiksa.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Saya mulakan sertraline 25mg sehari, seminggu, then increase to 50mg. First week mungkin rasa gelisah sikit, that's normal.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Bila saya boleh drive balik?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Mula dengan jarak dekat, isteri duduk sebelah. Kurangkan Red Bull perlahan-lahan. Jumpa saya dua minggu lagi.

patient_persona.description: Chew Kah Loong, 41, male, operations supervisor at a freight warehouse in Shah Alam; fourteen months of constant worry after a company merger; jaw tension, cracked molar, poor sleep; drinks beer nightly to sleep. First visit, at his wife's urging. Tense, fast Malaysian Mandarin with English workplace terms.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Haslinda binti Mohd Ali, Malay woman in her 40s, family medicine specialist in Shah Alam. Grounded, empathic; English-leaning, speaks functional Mandarin.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Mr. Chew，你太太叫你来，那你自己觉得怎样？Honestly。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 我自己也知道有问题。一整天都在担心，公司 merger 以后怕被裁员，担心钱，担心孩子，停不下来。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 这样多久了？

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 一年多了。晚上躺下，脑子一直转。Dentist 说我咬牙咬到牙齿 crack 了。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 除了担心，身体有没有其他感觉？肩膀紧，palpitation，拉肚子？

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 肩膀和下巴一直很 tight。脾气也变差，常常对孩子大声，marah-marah。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 你太太说你晚上喝 beer 帮助睡觉，大概多少？

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 两三罐，有时候四罐。不喝睡不着 lah。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 我明白你想 relax。但是 alcohol 会让 sleep 变浅，第二天更 anxious，变成一个 vicious cycle。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 你的 GAD-7 是 16，这是 generalised anxiety disorder。持续的担心，影响睡眠、工作和家庭。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 我以为是男人正常的 stress。我爸爸以前也这样，从来不看 doctor。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Stress 是正常的，但是一年多停不下来，就需要 treatment。好消息是，效果很好。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 我建议 escitalopram 10mg，每天早上。加上 CBT，学习处理担心的方法。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 吃这个药可以喝酒吗？周末一两罐也不行？

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 最好不要。至少先减到一罐，慢慢 stop。睡前半小时不要看公司的 WhatsApp group，jangan tengok phone。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 这个很难，老板半夜也会发 message。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 可以试着设一个时间，十点后手机放客厅。牙齿的问题，请牙医做一个 night guard。四个礼拜后回来。

condition: Social anxiety disorder in a new graduate

patient_persona.description: Nisha a/p Balakrishnan, 24, female, accounting graduate in Kuala Lumpur, unemployed eight months; freezes and blanks out in interviews and group settings. First visit. Soft, hesitant Malaysian Indian English with some Malay.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Benjamin Lim Zhi Hao, Malaysian Chinese man in his 30s, psychiatrist at a Kuala Lumpur hospital clinic. Gentle, patient; English.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Nisha, thanks for coming. Take your time. What made you decide to come today?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: I've failed eleven job interviews, doctor. Every time, muka jadi merah, my voice shakes, I forget everything. My amma thinks I'm not trying.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: That sounds exhausting. Is it only interviews, or other situations too?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Also presentations in uni, makan depan orang, even ordering at the mamak. I let my friends order for me.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: What goes through your mind before these situations?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: That they will see I'm nervous and think I'm bodoh. I replay it for days after.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: How long has this been going on?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Since sekolah menengah. But after graduation it's become worse, because I can't avoid it anymore.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: What you're describing sounds like social anxiety disorder. It's more than shyness, and it's very treatable.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Really? I thought memang dari lahir I'm like this.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Many people feel that way. The most effective treatment is CBT, where you learn to challenge the fears and gradually face situations step by step.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: We can also add a medicine, sertraline, starting 25mg daily and increasing. It usually takes four to six weeks to help.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: For the interviews, ada ubat to stop the shaking?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Propranolol 10mg, one hour before an interview, can reduce shaking and a racing heart. It doesn't treat the fear itself, but some people find it helpful. Let's check your asthma history first.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: No asthma. Okay, I want to try both. Can the CBT be in Tamil? Bila nervous, my English jadi blank.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: I'll ask our psychology team, and boleh juga guna Bahasa Melayu. See you in four weeks.

patient_persona.description: Ang Pei Shan, 36, female, bank branch officer in Johor Bahru who commutes across the Causeway; panic disorder on sertraline 50mg for four weeks; a private clinic gave alprazolam which she now takes daily. Follow-up. Fast, anxious Malaysian Mandarin mixed with Malay and English.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Mohd Zaki bin Hussin, Malay man in his 40s, psychiatrist at a Johor Bahru hospital. Calm, clear; English-leaning, speaks Mandarin phrases and Malay.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Pei Shan，sertraline 吃了四个礼拜，panic attack 有少一点吗？

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 少一点，以前一个礼拜五次，现在两三次。但是过 Causeway 塞车的时候，一定会来。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 塞在桥上，出不去，这种地方最容易触发。你现在 alprazolam 还在吃吗？

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 每天都吃，早上一粒，晚上一粒。没有它我不敢出门 lah，doktor。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 我明白，它很快有效，所以很依赖。但是每天吃，会 tolerance，越吃越需要，而且 stop 的时候 anxiety 会 rebound。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 可是我怕没有它，在桥上 attack 怎么办？

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 我们不会马上停。先把 sertraline 加到 100mg，它才是真正 treat panic 的。然后 alprazolam every two weeks 减一点。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 要减多久？几个月？

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 大概两三个月。慢慢减比较 safe，太快可能会晕，睡不着，甚至 seizure。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 塞车的时候，你可以做 breathing，或者听 podcast，转移注意力。CBT 也会教你面对这种情况。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: CBT 我有 appointment 下个月。医生，我老板问我为什么常常请假。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 你不需要讲细节。我可以给你一封信，只写 medical condition under treatment。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 好，谢谢。其实我很怕同事知道我看 psychiatry。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 这是你的 privacy，我们会保密。很多 professional 都在看我们，你一点都不孤单。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 听你这样讲，我安心一点。Terima kasih, doctor.

condition: Anxiety with palpitations, thyroid results review

patient_persona.description: Rahmah binti Yusof, 50, female, government office clerk in Alor Setar, Kedah; perimenopausal; palpitations and constant worry for five months; afraid of heart disease. Results review. Nervous, fast northern Malay.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Tan Beng Lee, Malaysian Chinese man in his 50s, GP in Alor Setar for many years. Grandfatherly, reassuring; speaks fluent northern Malay with English terms.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Puan Rahmah, keputusan darah dah keluar. Tiroid normal, darah tak kurang, gula pun normal. ECG dan Holter 24 jam pun normal.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Betul ke, doktor? Tapi jantung saya berdebar-debar hampir setiap hari. Saya takut ada sakit jantung macam arwah abang.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Holter tu rekod jantung sepanjang hari, termasuk masa puan rasa berdebar. At that time, your heart was a bit fast but normal rhythm.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Kalau jantung OK, kenapa saya rasa macam ni? Tak faham saya.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Puan pernah cakap puan risau banyak benda. Masih macam tu? Worry sangat?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Ya, doktor. Risau anak kat universiti, risau kerja, risau duit. Malam fikir, tak boleh tidur. Kadang-kadang peluh, badan panas.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Haid macam mana sekarang? Masih datang teratur?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Tak tentu dah, dua tiga bulan sekali, irregular. Kawan kata saya dah nak menopaus.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Menopause can cause hot flushes, sweating and palpitations, dan buat anxiety lebih teruk. Dua-dua ni berkait.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Dari soal selidik tadi, score GAD-7 puan 13. Ini generalised anxiety, tahap sederhana. Boleh dirawat.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Kena makan ubat ke? Saya tak nak ketagih.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Kita boleh mula dengan kaunseling dan teknik relaksasi. Kalau tak cukup, ada ubat yang tak ketagih, macam sertraline.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Saya cuba kaunseling dulu, doktor.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Baik. Kurangkan kopi petang, jalan kaki pagi. Kalau hot flushes dan berpeluh teruk sangat, kita boleh bincang HRT, rawatan menopaus. Datang balik sebulan.

condition: Chronic insomnia after bereavement in perimenopause

patient_persona.description: Evelyn Chua Siew Hong, 47, female, secondary school English teacher in Petaling Jaya; eighteen months of poor sleep since her mother died; night sweats; drives 35 minutes to school. First visit. Articulate, weary Malaysian Chinese English.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Arif Hakim bin Zulkifli, Malay man in his 40s, family medicine specialist with a sleep interest in Petaling Jaya. Thoughtful, methodical; English-leaning.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Doctor, I haven't slept properly for a year and a half. I take an hour to fall asleep, then terjaga at two or three, hot and heart racing, and I'm up for good by four thirty.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: When did this start?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: After my mother passed away. I jaga her for months. Lepas pengebumian, I just couldn't switch off.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: I'm sorry for your loss. How are you during the day? Sleepy while driving?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Exhausted, but not sleepy exactly. Once I tertidur at a traffic light, that scared me.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: That's important for safety. Any snoring, or stopping breathing at night?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: My husband says tak berdengkur. But I wake up drenched, and my periods are irregular now.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Night sweats and irregular periods suggest perimenopause, which can disturb sleep. Grief too. And then worry about sleep keeps it going.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: A friend gave me zolpidem, I took it maybe five times. Senang, should I just take that?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Short-term it can help, but long-term it loses effect and can cause dependence and next-day drowsiness, not good before driving.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: The best evidence is for CBT for insomnia. It includes a sleep schedule, getting out of bed if awake more than twenty minutes, and no clock-watching.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Get out of bed? I thought I should just baring there and rest.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Lying awake trains your brain to link bed with being awake. Keep bed for sleep only. Fixed wake time, even weekends.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: For the night sweats, we can discuss hormone therapy. And would you like a referral to talk about your mother? Grief counselling helps.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Yes, I think I need that. I never really had time to grieve, 一直在忙.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Keep a sleep diary for two weeks, and don't drive when you feel drowsy. Come back and we'll plan the next step.

condition: Insomnia in a shift worker using antihistamines

patient_persona.description: Shahrul Nizam bin Ahmad, 40, male, production line leader at a factory in Kulim, Kedah, on rotating shifts; takes chlorpheniramine from the pharmacy to sleep. First visit. Rough, direct northern Malay with English work words.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Loo Pei Kee, Malaysian Chinese woman in her 30s, GP in Kulim. Practical, brisk; English-leaning, fluent northern Malay.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Doktor, saya tak boleh tidur dah berbulan. Shift pusing setiap minggu, pagi, petang, malam. Badan dah tak tahu bila nak tidur.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Lepas shift malam, balik rumah tidur pukul berapa?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Balik pukul lapan pagi, tidur pukul sembilan. Tapi pukul dua belas dah terjaga, bising anak, bising traffic.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Selama ni ada ambil apa-apa untuk tidur? Sleeping pill?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Beli ubat selesema yang kuning tu, chlorpheniramine. Makan dua biji, baru boleh lelap. Dah enam bulan.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Ubat tu memang buat mengantuk, tapi lama-lama badan dah biasa, kesan kurang. Esok pagi rasa berat kepala tak?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Ya, macam mamai. Masa jaga mesin, kadang-kadang lambat nak react.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Itu bahaya kat kilang, encik. Ubat tu kita stop. For shift workers, the most important thing is the bedroom.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Bilik gelap, guna langsir tebal atau penutup mata. Pakai earplug. Beritahu keluarga, pukul sembilan sampai tiga petang tu masa tidur.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Anak kecil, doktor. Susah nak senyap.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Faham. Mungkin isteri boleh bawa anak keluar sekejap waktu pagi. Jangan minum kopi lepas pukul empat pagi masa shift malam.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Kopi tu yang buat saya segar masa shift!

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Minum awal shift, bukan hujung. Balik kerja, wear sunglasses, kurangkan cahaya pagi supaya badan tak ingat dah siang.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Boleh minta tukar shift tak, doktor? Saya dah tak larat.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Saya boleh tulis surat cadangkan shift rotate ke depan, pagi ke petang ke malam, dan tak tukar terlalu cepat. Datang balik tiga minggu.

condition: Insomnia with long-term hypnotic use and falls

patient_persona.description: Foo Ah Seng, 78, male, retired goldsmith in Ipoh; on lorazepam 1mg nightly for twelve years from a private clinic; one fall last month. Refill visit. Stubborn, slow Cantonese-coloured Malaysian Mandarin.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Ong Kah Yee, Malaysian Chinese woman in her 30s, family medicine specialist at an Ipoh health clinic. Gentle, persistent; English-leaning, fluent Mandarin and some Cantonese.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 医生，我来拿睡觉的药，lorazepam。吃了十二年，不吃睡不着。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 符伯，我看到你上个月跌倒了，是晚上起来的时候吗？

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 对，半夜去 toilet，脚软软的，跌在走廊。还好只是手瘀。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 这个药会让老人家晚上站不稳，早上也会比较 blur，fall risk 高很多，jatuh sekali nanti patah tulang。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 可是吃了那么多年，都没事啊，doctor。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 年轻的时候身体处理得快。七十几岁，药在身体里留得比较久。上个月的跌倒，可能就是这个原因。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 那你要我马上停？我一定睡不着。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 不是马上停。突然停很危险。我们用两三个月，慢慢减少，每两个礼拜减四分之一粒。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 减少了，睡不着怎么办？Insomnia 怎么办？

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 刚开始可能睡得少一点，这是正常的。老人家本来就睡五六个钟头，不需要睡八个钟头。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 你白天做什么？会不会在椅子上睡很久？

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 下午看 TV，常常睡两三个钟头。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 那晚上当然睡不着。下午 nap 不要超过半小时，早上去 taman 散步，晒太阳。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 以前我会跟朋友去 kopitiam 喝早茶，现在他们很多都不在了。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 那可以试试 community centre 的活动，也可以认识新朋友。有朋友聊天，晚上也会比较好睡。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 好吧，我试试。但是你不要一下子全部拿掉。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 我答应你，慢慢来。两个礼拜后回来，我们一起看怎样。

condition: Insomnia with anxiety in a young adult

patient_persona.description: Nur Atiqah binti Jaafar, 26, female, junior executive at a tour agency in Kota Kinabalu, Sabah; can't fall asleep, scrolls her phone until 3 a.m.; worried about job contract renewal. First visit. Soft, quick Sabah Malay with English.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Wilfred Sipaun, Kadazan man in his 40s, GP in Kota Kinabalu. Friendly, down-to-earth; English-leaning, speaks Sabah Malay.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Doktor, saya susah mau tidur. Baring pukul sebelas, tapi pukul tiga pagi baru lelap. Pagi pula kena bangun pukul enam.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Masa baring tu, apa yang Atiqah buat? Fikir apa? Any worries?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Main phone lah, scroll TikTok. Kalau letak phone, fikir pasal kontrak kerja, takut tak disambung.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Kontrak tu bila habis?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Dua bulan lagi. Bos belum cakap apa-apa. Saya risau, family harap saya bantu duit rumah.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Faham, memang berat, stressful. Siang pula, minum kopi atau teh berapa kali?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Kopi pagi, teh tarik petang, kadang-kadang Milo ais malam.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Teh tarik petang tu ada caffeine, it can stay in your body until night. Cuba stop lepas pukul dua petang.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Phone tu, cahaya skrin buat otak rasa masih siang. Satu jam sebelum tidur, letak phone jauh dari katil, charge kat luar bilik.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Susah bah, doktor. Tapi saya cuba.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Kalau dah dua puluh minit tak lelap, bangun, duduk kat luar, baca buku atau dengar muzik perlahan. Bila mengantuk, baru masuk bilik.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Boleh bagi ubat tidur sikit, doktor? Kawan saya makan melatonin.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Melatonin 2mg boleh cuba short-term, one hour before bed. Tapi yang penting tabiat tidur tadi.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Risau pasal kerja tu, kalau makin teruk, sampai berdebar atau tak lalu makan, datang jumpa saya lagi. Kita boleh refer kaunselor.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: OK, doktor. Thank you sebab tak cakap saya manja.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Tak manja langsung. Datang balik tiga minggu, bawa diari tidur.

condition: Insomnia with suspected obstructive sleep apnoea

patient_persona.description: Yap Chee Keong, 58, male, e-hailing driver in Kuantan, Pahang, driving ten hours a day; wakes many times at night, loud snoring, sleepy at the wheel; hypertension. Results review of sleep diary. Talkative, hoarse Malaysian Mandarin mixed with Malay and English.

doctor_persona.description: Dr. Norhafizah binti Rahim, Malay woman in her 40s, family medicine specialist at a Kuantan clinic. Direct, caring; English-leaning, speaks simple Mandarin and fluent Malay.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 叶先生，你的 sleep diary 我看了。你一个晚上醒来五六次，对吗？

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 对，每次醒来都好像喘不过气，要坐起来。老婆说我打呼很大声，像 lori 一样。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 她有没有看到你睡觉的时候 stop breathing？

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 有，她说我会停一下，然后突然很大声吸气。她很怕，常常摇醒我。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 白天开车的时候，会不会想睡？

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 会 lah，doktor。下午等客的时候常常睡着。有一次等红灯，后面的车 hon 我才醒。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 这个很危险，对你和乘客都是。你的 neck 很粗，BMI 是 31，血压也难控制。这些都指向 obstructive sleep apnoea。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Sleep apnoea？不是失眠吗？我以为要吃安眠药。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Sleeping pills 会让 apnoea 更严重，千万不要吃。你睡不好，是因为 breathing 一直停，brain 被叫醒。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 那要怎样医？Ada ubat 吗？

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 先做 sleep study，在医院睡一个晚上。如果确认，最有效是 CPAP machine，睡觉时戴一个面罩。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 那个 machine 很贵吧？我每天要 drive 赚钱的。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 有几种价钱，hospital 也可以帮忙 apply subsidy。减重也会帮很多，lose five to ten kilos 就不一样。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 在 sleep study 之前，如果开车觉得困，一定要停下来，jangan paksa。不要喝酒，侧睡，床头高一点。

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: 好，我会注意。我太太会很高兴，她终于可以 tidur lena 了。

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: 我现在写 referral。两个礼拜内会有 appointment。血压的药继续吃。
